cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his beloved child (2 Timothy 1:1-2). He just told Timothy to be kind to everyone and to gently correct the people who oppose him (2 Timothy 2:24-25). Now Paul says, "But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come."

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy that terrible times will come in the last days. What does he say will make them so terrible?

cards.text: So Paul starts a list, and friend, this list does NOT quit: lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy.
He's STILL going: unloving, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, without love of good, traitorous, reckless, conceited. And I thought MY mustache went on forever.

cards.question: Paul's list started with people who love themselves and love money. Near the end, he says they'll be lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of who?

cards.text: Now hold on, friend. Because here comes the twist.

cards.question: Paul says the people on this list have a form of godliness.

cards.text: They have a form of godliness, but they deny its power. That's a cookie box with a perfect gold bow on top, and you open it up and it's just... crumbs.

cards.question: These people have a form of godliness but deny its power. What does Paul tell Timothy to do about people like these?

cards.text: Paul says they're the kind who worm their way into households. They captivate vulnerable women who are weighed down with sins and led astray by various passions.

cards.question: Paul says these women are always learning. What's the catch?

answers.text: They never come to know the truth
They never share what they learn
They forget it all by morning

cards.text: Always learning, never getting there: that's me reading the same cookie recipe every night for a year and STILL asking which one's the oven. Then Paul reaches way back for two names: Jannes and Jambres.

cards.question: Paul compares these men to Jannes and Jambres. Jannes and Jambres opposed ___.
Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, Israel's leader. Paul says these men oppose the ___ in the same way.

cards.text: Paul doesn't tiptoe around it, friend. He says these men are depraved in mind.

cards.question: Paul says these men still stand approved in the faith.

cards.text: Worming into homes. Opposing the truth. Sounds like nobody can stop these guys, right? Hold on. Paul's got one more thing to say.

cards.question: Paul says these men will keep advancing further and further.
Just like with Jannes and Jambres, Paul says these men's folly will be ___ to everyone.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from the passage. 'Now hold on, friend. Because here comes the twist.' is only a teaser. It cites 2 Timothy 3:5 but uses none of that verse, which is told only on cards 7 and 8.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites 2 Timothy 3:5, but it tells no part of that verse.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'Worming into homes. Opposing the truth.' recaps verses 6 and 8. The rest of the card is a teaser. It tells nothing from 2 Timothy 3:9, the verse it cites.
The card cites 2 Timothy 3:9, but it tells no part of that verse. The content it does use comes from verses 6 and 8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup 'Sounds like nobody can stop these guys, right? Hold on.' signals the twist that they will be stopped. That rules out True on card 18's statement 'Paul says these men will keep advancing further and further.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Jannes and Jambres show up for the first time here, but nothing says who they are. The only thing Scripture says about them is that they opposed Moses (2 Timothy 3:8). Card 13 asks exactly that, so saying who they are would give the answer away. Calling them Pharaoh's magicians comes from tradition, not from the text.
findings.question: When the only Bible fact about a new person is the answer to a later choice card, should the 'New people' rule give way to 'Never give away an answer', or should the card be restructured, for example by telling the Moses link on the story card and asking about something else?
